import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided by the user
data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Create a figure with subplots to visualize the distributions of the key features
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
fig.suptitle('Transaction Data Overview', fontsize=16)

# Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amount
sns.histplot(df['amount'], kde=True, ax=axes[0], color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Amount')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Frequency')

# Plot 2: Distribution of Hour of Day
# Use discrete bins for hours (0-23)
sns.histplot(df['hour_of_day'], bins=range(0, 25), ax=axes[1], color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black')
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Hour of Day')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day (0-23)')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Frequency')
axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 4)) # Set ticks for better readability

# Plot 3: Count of Transaction Types
sns.countplot(x='transaction_type', data=df, ax=axes[2], palette='viridis', order=df['transaction_type'].value_counts().index)
axes[2].set_title('Count of Transaction Types')
axes[2].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axes[2].set_ylabel('Count')
